column12:
1. There was no meaningful discussion on governance and guardrails for autonomous AI. Everyone showed enthusiasm for agentic workflows, but no one covered ownership, approval paths, risk controls, or rollback policies. Without that, AI-at-scale is a liability.

2. Data architecture and system-of-record strategy was avoided. The roadmap assumes unified context exists, but didn’t address the operational work needed to align taxonomies, ticket fields, knowledge structure, and identity management across business units.

3. Commercial and change-management implications were brushed aside. AI impact on FTE distribution, licensing models, admin workload, and training budgets was not discussed, yet those will determine ROI far more than feature releases.

The implementation of RBAC. Understanding how this is going to have ripple effects within the tool would have been really helpful as it's going to impact all customers and it sounds like the team weren't too sure on what work would need to be done by us as customers.

Give this is a big change it could involve a lot of work for the app owners/admins and getting permissions wrong could result in down time for our agents and tickets coming in to us.

This is something that I think needs to be mandatory as historically big changes and upgrades to the system have been detrimental to customers and seemingly not well planned. Demonstrating the due-diligence and giving a bit of confidence to the customers for these items would go a long way and eventually wouldn't be required after that confidence has been gained.
